input: Research shared allotment plots near me

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Without knowing the user's location, it is impossible to identify relevant allotment schemes, councils, or community groups nearby.
Shared allotments can mean co-renting a plot with others, community garden membership, or council-run sharing schemes — the type determines where to look.
Whether this is for a solo person wanting to share with strangers, an existing group looking for a plot, or a family unit changes the search approach entirely.
Budget for rental fees or membership costs will filter out schemes that are too expensive or steer toward free community options.
How far the user is willing to travel sets the practical radius for the search and affects which councils or sites are relevant.
Some users prioritise specific growing goals (vegetables, flowers, etc.) or community aspects (social events, beginner-friendly), which shapes which plots to shortlist.
Knowing whether the end goal is a compiled shortlist, a single recommendation, or actually joining a plot determines how deep the research needs to go.

gold.taskTitle: Research shared allotment plots near me
gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate shared allotment plot options in the user's local area.

questions.title: What town, city, or postcode should the search centre on?
questions.description: Establish the user's location so the research can target the right local councils, allotment associations, and community gardens.

questions.title: What type of sharing arrangement are you looking for?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants to co-rent a plot with strangers, join a community garden, or find a council-run plot-sharing scheme, as each has different search routes.

questions.title: Are you searching alone or with a ready-made group?
questions.description: Determine whether the user needs to be matched with other plot-sharers or already has people in mind, which affects which platforms and schemes to target.

questions.title: What is your maximum monthly or annual budget for plot fees?
questions.description: Identify a cost ceiling so that free community options, subsidised council plots, or paid private sites can be prioritised accordingly.

questions.title: How far are you willing to travel to reach the plot?
questions.description: Set a practical distance or travel-time radius to filter results and avoid shortlisting sites that are impractical to visit regularly.

questions.title: What do you most want to grow or get out of the allotment?
questions.description: Understand whether the priority is vegetables, flowers, social community, beginner guidance, or something else, to match the right type of plot or scheme.

questions.title: What does a successful outcome of this research look like?
questions.description: Establish whether the user wants a ranked shortlist of options, a single best recommendation, or a step-by-step plan to actually join a plot.
